svg.text: TWO QUESTIONS · ONE CONNECTED INVESTIGATION
Navigation proposal — new diagnostic charts and record detail are not implemented yet.
LEVEL 1 · OVERVIEW
Finding: Trousers 688 / 2,435 = 28.25% vs overall 1,660 / 7,257 = 22.87%.
Question: which products/sizes and reported reasons deserve investigation?
Entry context: Oct 2025–Sep 2026 · Trousers · All products · All sizes
LEVEL 2A · PRODUCTS & SIZES
WHERE are returns concentrated?
Dimensions: product × size; original sale-period filters.
Measures: returned units, sold units, rate and refunds.
Charts: returned-unit ranking + rate/count heatmap.
Fact grain: one sales line, safely aggregated.
Next: sales-line evidence list → sale_line_id.
LEVEL 2B · RETURN REASONS
WHAT was reported; how does its mix vary?
Dimensions: reason/group × original sale month.
Measures: returned units and shares; fixed cohort base.
Charts: reason counts + monthly 100% reason mix.
Fact grain: one accepted returned-unit record.
Next: return evidence list → return_id / sale_line_id.
↔ Same shared context ↔
LEVEL 3 · SUPPORTING SALES LINE & LINKED RETURNS
Show existing keys: sale_line_id and linked return_id; product, size, sale/delivery dates,
units sold, return dates/reasons, returned units and refunds. Highlight the selected return.
This needs a new bounded read-only record endpoint; the current API exposes aggregates.
CONTEXT AND COMPARISON CONTRACT
Shared original-sale period/category/product/size travel across both diagnostics. Chart selections remain visible.
Product/size rates = returned / sold. Reason shares = returned units for a reason / all cohort returns.
Local reason/month evidence selections never shrink sold-unit denominators or change headline cohort KPIs.
Back restores the saved parent URL, filters, local selection and focus. Overview restores its saved entry context.
